chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, they raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
It was from the supplication of my father (peace be upon him) regarding the newly-occurring matters: 'O Allah! Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad.'

And Forgive me, and Be Merciful to me, and Purify my deeds, and Ease my return, and Guide my heart, and Secure my fear, and Grant me good health in my life-time, all of it, and Affirm my proofs, and Forgive my mistakes, and Whiten my face, and Safeguard me in my Religion, and Ease my seeking (for livelihood), and Expand upon me regarding my sustenance for I am weak.
And Overlook from my evil deeds what are with me by the Goodness with what is with You, and do not Grieve me for myself nor Grieve me for my intimate friends.
And Grant me, O my God, an opportunity from Your Opportunities Removing with it from me the entirety of what I am afflicted with, and Return upon me what is better Ways with me.
For my strength has weakened, and my reasons are scarce, and my hopes from Your creatures are cut off, and there does not remain except hoping in You, and reliance upon You and Your Power upon me.
O Lord! If You are Merciful to me and Grant good health to me, is like Your Power upon me if You were to Punish me and Afflict me.
My God! Mentioning Your Rewards comforts me, and the hoping for Your Bounties strengthens me, and I have not been isolated from Your Bounties since the day You Created me.
And You are my Lord, and my Master, and my Defender, and my Shelter, and the Protector for me, and the Lenient to me, and the Merciful with me, and the Guarantor of my sustenance.

And in Your Ordainment and Your Power is everything what I am in, therefore let it happen to be, O my Chief and my Master, regarding what You Judge, and You Ordain, and You Finalise, hasten my finishing from what I am in, the entirety of it, and the good health for me.
For I cannot find anyone to repel that apart from You, nor do I rely with regards to it upon anyone except You.

Therefore be, O the One with the Majesty and the Benevolence, during the goodness of my thoughts with You, my hope for you, and be Merciful on my desperation and my dependence, and the weakness of my (body) parts, and Favour with that upon me and upon every supplicant who supplicates You, O Most Merciful of the merciful ones, and Send Salawat upon Muhammad and his Progeny.

key_terms.ذُو الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَام: The One with Majesty and Benevolence
key_terms.صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Send Salawat upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for distress and newly occurring matters in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication (Dua al-Hajah) is traditionally recited when facing new difficulties, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *tawassul* through the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt while acknowledging human frailty (*da'f*) against divine power. It structurally moves from petitioning for specific relief to a profound theological assertion that hope in God's habitual grace (*'awaid*) outweighs fear of His punishment, a concept deeply rooted in Shia devotional practice.
